source: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide 2.0, ILAE 2017 Classification, WHO Emergency Triage Guidelines

adults_generalised_tonic_clonic.avoid_reason_wra: Teratogenic — associated with neural tube defects and neurodevelopmental impairment in offspring. Contraindicated in women of reproductive age unless no alternatives and effective contraception in place.

phenobarbital.notes: Most affordable AED in LMIC. Strong CYP3A4/CYP2C9 inducer — significant ARV and TB drug interactions.

sodium_valproate.notes: Monitor LFTs. Teratogenic — neural tube defects. Avoid in women of reproductive age.

carbamazepine.notes: CYP3A4 inducer (auto-induction). Reduces rifampicin efficacy and ARV levels. Monitor Na — risk of hyponatraemia.

phenytoin.notes: Non-linear kinetics — small dose increases can cause toxicity. INH inhibits CYP2C9 → phenytoin toxicity risk.

lamotrigine.notes: Preferred for women of reproductive age. Slow titration required to reduce SJS risk.

drug_interactions.effect: Phenobarbital reduces ARV plasma levels by 30–75% → virological failure risk
drug_interactions.management: Avoid combination where possible. If unavoidable: switch to integrase inhibitor-based ART (dolutegravir — less affected). Monitor viral load closely.

drug_interactions.effect: Phenobarbital levels may decrease; rifampicin efficacy maintained but monitor phenobarb levels
drug_interactions.management: Monitor clinical seizure control. Check phenobarbital drug level after starting TB therapy.

drug_interactions.effect: CBZ plasma levels reduced 50–70% — seizure breakthrough risk
drug_interactions.management: Increase CBZ dose with close drug level monitoring. Consider switching AED during TB treatment.

drug_interactions.effect: CBZ levels may increase (ritonavir inhibits CYP3A4) or decrease — unpredictable
drug_interactions.management: Prefer alternative AED. If combined: measure CBZ level and titrate carefully.

drug_interactions.effect: Phenytoin toxicity (nystagmus, ataxia, confusion) at therapeutic doses
drug_interactions.management: Monitor phenytoin level within 2 weeks of starting INH. Reduce phenytoin dose if level elevated.

drug_interactions.effect: VPA levels reduced up to 75% — seizure risk
drug_interactions.management: Monitor VPA level after starting lopinavir/ritonavir. May need dose increase.

drug_interactions.effect: Lamotrigine levels double — toxicity risk (dizziness, diplopia, SJS)
drug_interactions.management: Halve lamotrigine starting dose and titrate more slowly when combined with VPA.

status_epilepticus_protocol.definition: Seizure lasting ≥5 minutes OR ≥2 seizures without recovery of consciousness

phases.action: Position patient, protect airway, O2, IV access, glucose check

phases.dose_adult: 10mg IV over 2 min OR 10–20mg rectal (if no IV)
phases.repeat: May repeat once after 5 min if seizure continues

phases.note: Phenytoin 20mg/kg IV at ≤50 mg/min if phenobarb unavailable

phases.action: Refer urgently to ICU. Intubation + anaesthesia (propofol/midazolam/thiopentone)

monitoring: LFT monthly for first 6 months then 6-monthly
FBC and Na at baseline and 3-monthly

wra_aed_safety.notes: All AEDs except lamotrigine reduce OCP efficacy via CYP induction. Advise barrier contraception. Folic acid 5mg daily for all women of reproductive age on AEDs.

follow_up_schedule.newly_diagnosed: 2 weeks, then 1 month, then 3-monthly until stable
follow_up_schedule.seizure_free_2_years: Annual review, discuss AED withdrawal (specialist decision)
follow_up_schedule.drug_level_monitoring: At baseline, 4 weeks after dose change, then annually or with clinical change
